Here you can find some of my favorite resources for statistics and coding in R. All credit for the work contained in these materials goes to the original authors.

## R and R Studio {.exp-heading .accent-1}

### Online Textbooks {.exp-heading .accent-1}

::: {.exp-stack}

::: {.exp-card .accent-1}
### [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/)

I used this book when I was learning R for the first time. It is a great resource for learning how to import, tidy, and visualize data.
:::

::: {.exp-card .accent-1}
### [What They Forgot to Teach You About R](https://rstats.wtf/)

Build good data hygiene habits by following the guidelines in this book.
:::

::: {.exp-card .accent-1}
### [ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis](https://ggplot2-book.org/)

A fantastic overview about the "Grammar of Graphics" that ggplot uses. This book is a great foundational guide for building figures in R.  
:::

::: {.exp-card .accent-1}
### [R Graphics Cookbook](https://r-graphics.org/index.html)

Find more advanced and specific recipes to up your visualization game!
:::
:::

### My Favorite Packages {.exp-heading .accent-1}

::: {.exp-stack}

::: {.exp-card .accent-2}
### [modelsummary](https://modelsummary.com/vignettes/get_started.html)

You can create publication ready, APA-style tables with this package in just a few lines of code.

:::

::: {.exp-card .accent-2}
### [easystats](https://easystats.github.io/easystats/)

*easystats* is a collection of packages that help interpret model outputs.

:::

:::

## Statistics {.exp-heading .accent-1}

::: {.exp-stack}

::: {.exp-card .accent-3}
### [UCLA’s Office of Advanced Research Computing](https://stats.oarc.ucla.edu/other/mult-pkg/seminars/#R)

Offers a wealth of free resources that explain both the statistical concepts and code for a variety of methods. 
:::
:::
